newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS - C-C Amatil unveils Philippines impact.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - C-C Amatil unveils Philippines impact.

text.p: Soft drink bottler Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd showed the impact of its latest acquisition on Wednesday, boosting its net profit by A$40 million from three months of trading in the Philippines.
However, sales revenue growth in Europe for the first half ended June 30 was below expectations and the company warned floods there could adversely impact the second half.

C-C Amatil, which is 33 percent owned by The Coca-Cola Co, posted an interim net profit, excluding Philppines earnings, of A$58.1 million, in line with forecasts of around A$60 million and steady on A$57.8 million a year earlier.

However, net profit jumped to A$98.1 million with the inclusion of three months trading figures from Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc, acquired in a A$3.4 billion share swap deal with Philippines giant San Miguel Corp in April.
The jump reflected the far higher margins achieved by the Philippines operation, which in calendar 1996 earned profits similar to C-C Amatil but on sales revenues a third the size.

C-C Amatil was also buoyed by a 19 percent rise in sales volumes in the Philippines operations over the three months to June 30, while trading profit margins eased slightly to a still strong 18 percent.
"We're very excited about the strong volume growth ... and margins have been maintained and that's a tremendous result," C-C Amatil's chief financial officer Mike Ihlein told Reuters.
The outlook for operations for the rest of the year remained strong, the company said.
In Europe, which provides about a third of sales revenue, sales volumes grew 12 percent, but sales revenue rose two percent and trading profits three percent.
C-C Amatil said the results had been affected by currency movements, subdued market conditions in some countries and poor weather in April and June.
Managing director Norb Cole said revenue was lagging sales volume, but had improved on the latter part of 1996.
"The market is moving in the right direction to get improved revenue results and we would expect that to continue to improve over the balance of this year," he said.
Prices were increasing in a number of key markets, for both Coca-Cola and its competitors.

However, Cole said sales volumes in Europe "haven't been very good" over the first five weeks of the second half due to the impact of the floods, which have washed out roads and washed out or isolated some facilities.
It was still too early to quantify the likely impact of the flooding.
"The waters haven't receded and we haven't even been able to get back into some parts of the marketplace so we don't know what the full impact is going to be," Cole said.
Elsewhere, he expected the appointment of a fourth, independent director by San Miguel to the C-C Amatil board to be clarified in October.
San Miguel, which has a 25 percent stake in the bottler, appointed three of its four directors last month.
